subject: First-byte SLO & streaming chunk cadence — post-call recap and plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@finservplus.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: First-byte SLO & streaming chunk cadence — post-call recap and plan

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Time-to-first-byte / Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: p95 <= 80 ms, p99 goal <= 200 ms for 95% of interactive web sessions.
- Response patterns: mix of short (<= 120 tokens) and medium (300–600 tokens) responses; streaming is mandatory for the web UI.
- Streaming delivery: prefer SSE for progressive updates to the front-end; fallback to WebSocket acceptable for high-concurrency mobile clients.
- Chunk cadence: customer-visible update cadence should be ~60–120 ms per chunk for a smooth typing UX (we heard 70 ms preferred in the demo).
- Throughput/concurrency: steady peak ~200 concurrent active streams, burstable to 350 for minute-level spikes; sustained QPS target ~220 requests/sec during peak.
- Deployment: production workload will run in us-east-1; FinServPlus will use a VPC/private deployment but wants a Hosted/Dedicated pilot first.

Open clarifying items we promised to follow up on:
1) Model baseline: please confirm the model family (you mentioned a tuned Llama-2 variant) and an approximate token-per-response distribution for the sample prompts.
2) Network constraints: are there strict client IP allowlist requirements or proxies that add TLS handshake latency?
3) Acceptance criteria: do we agree on p95 TTFT <= 80 ms and visible chunk cadence <= 120 ms for sign-off?

Proposed next steps (what we'll do on our side):
- Share a short perf test plan and temporary test credentials (we'll need allowlist IPs). Attachments: redwood-ttft-profiles.csv (sample measurement targets) and sse-chunking-guidelines.pdf (implementation notes).
- Run a two-phase pilot: 
  Phase A - hosted Redwood API baseline with your prompt set (48–72 hour window, measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT and chunk cadence)
  Phase B - dedicated pool sizing and stress run with target concurrency and burst profile.
- Internal sizing recommendation (initial): Dedicated pool equivalent to 8x A100-class GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache warmup. We'll validate during Phase A.

If that looks right, I'll schedule the Phase A run for July 7–8 and loop in infra for allowlisting. Please confirm model name and share 20–30 representative prompts (anonymized is fine).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-ttft-profiles.csv, sse-chunking-guidelines.pdf
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@finservplus.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@finservplus.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: First-byte SLO & streaming chunk cadence — post-call recap and plan

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up. Confirming and adding a few constraints from our side: 

Confirmations:
- Model: we will be using an in-house fine-tuned Llama-2-70B variant (we can provide an S3 snapshot and HF-style config).
- Prompt mix: roughly 60% short answers (<120 tokens), 35% medium (120–450 tokens), 5% long (>450 tokens). Average generated tokens per request ~180.
- Target acceptance: p95 TTFT <= 100 ms is our minimal acceptable SLO (we'd prefer your 80 ms target if achievable); chunk cadence 70–150 ms is acceptable, but UX team prefers <= 100 ms when possible.
- Concurrency: steady 200 active streams; allow bursts to 350 for up to 3 minutes.

Constraints / callouts:
- We have an outbound proxy that adds ~20–30 ms TLS overhead in some regions; we'll provide network diagrams.
- Mobile client will use WebSocket for re-connections; web frontend will use SSE.
- Security: before any hosted pilot we need an NDA in place (I attached the standard vendor form) and a list of Redwood's SOC2 controls.

I'll attach the prompt sample and a small CSV with token-length histograms. We can accept July 7–8 for Phase A run — please send test endpoints and allowlist IPs by EOD July 3rd so our networking team can configure.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Engineering | FinServPlus
elaine.park@finservplus.com

Attachments: finserv-prompts-sample.csv, vendor-nda.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: First-byte SLO & streaming chunk cadence — post-call recap and plan

Looping in implementation details we need to prep on our side: 

Checklist for Phase A (hosted baseline):
- Prep perf harness: use customer's prompt set (Elaines's CSV) and synthesize realistic client connection patterns (200 steady, bursts to 350).
- Measure metrics: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), first-chunk latency, inter-chunk cadence distribution, tokens/sec, end-to-end TLS handshake time.
- Observability: enable per-request token timing (trace id), firehose logs to secure bucket for 7 days, and generate a CSV of chunk timestamps for UX team.
- Env: run in us-east-1, use dedicated testing pool with identical model binary/quantization as customer's planned deployment.
- Roll plan: if p95 TTFT > 120 ms, automatic fallback to a quantized variant and increased batching disabled for interactive streams.

Operational asks from sales/SE: 
- Jordan: send the allowlist IPs and the HubSpot deal link so I can attach the perf results.
- Marissa: please reserve a 8x A100-equivalent pool for July 7–8 and tag it FS-2026-073.

I'll prepare a short runbook and upload the mutual action plan (see attached).

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Great — thanks for the quick confirmations, Elaine. Action items and scheduling below: 

Action items for this week:
1) Redwood -> FinServPlus: test endpoints + temporary API keys, allowlist IPs (I'll send these by EOD 2026-07-03).
2) FinServPlus -> Redwood: model snapshot details, prompt CSV (received), network diagram (expected by EOD 2026-07-03).
3) Infra (Marissa): pool reservation for 2026-07-07 00:00 UTC - 2026-07-08 23:59 UTC, tagged FS-2026-073.
4) Legal: exchange NDA (Elaine attached vendor_nda.pdf) — I'll loop in our contracts team.

Scheduling: Phase A (hosted baseline) target window July 7–8. Vivek will run the harness and share a results summary within 24 hours of run completion (CSV with per-chunk timestamps + a short results PDF). If we meet p95 TTFT <= 100 ms and chunk cadence median <= 100 ms we will move to Phase B (dedicated sizing).

One more ask for network teams: can you confirm whether the proxy terminates TLS at the edge or passes through the client TLS? That affects our handshake budgeting.

I'll send the allowlist and test creds in a separate secure email. Thanks again — looking forward to the run.

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
